mission: The Ankhural Codex fragment recovered from the fortress — Sera unlocks it, and the group confronts the heretical framework: the Force lattice as imposed structure rather than natural property
why_now: The debate in Chapter 8 created the intellectual space; the Codex provides the theoretical framework that crystallizes the conflict
conflict: The Codex's argument is philosophically devastating — if the lattice is imposed, then light and dark aren't properties of the Force but a framework someone built. Everything the Jedi believe about moral intuition through the Force could be wrong.
turning_point: Touching the Codex provides experiential flashes — not information but sensation. Ben feels a moment of the Force without the lattice. It's not hostile. It's formless. The absence of moral intuition is terrifying not because it's dark, but because there's nothing there at all.
opening_hook: The Codex fragment has been sealed in its case since the fortress. When Sera opens it, the air in the common area changes — everyone Force-sensitive feels the artifact's resonance simultaneously.
closing_hook: Ship alarm. The next planned stop — the Brotherhood Outpost — has been breached. Energy readings spiking. Someone is there, or has been there very recently.
emotional_trajectory: Intellectual engagement -> existential vertigo -> sharp alarm

stakes.personal: Ben's foundational understanding of the Force challenged at the deepest level
stakes.interpersonal: Four Force-sensitives experiencing the same artifact, interpreting it four different ways
stakes.external: The Codex provides the theoretical framework for understanding the wound — and for exploiting it

setting: Aboard the Steady Returns — common area, the Codex fragment on the table between them
sensory_details: The Codex glowing faintly; experiential flash when Ben touches it — the Force present but unstructured, like hearing music with all the notes but no melody; each character's Force presence reacting differently to the artifact
action_beats: Sera breaks the seal on the Codex case and lifts the fragment onto the common area table
Ben touches the Codex and his hand jerks back — the experiential flash of unstructured Force hitting like sensory overload
The ship alarm cuts through the discussion and Desh clears the common area to reach the cockpit in three seconds
promises_planted: The Codex's theoretical framework has a real-world answer (PP14)
notes: R06 — the Codex's core argument. This is the intellectual heart of the novel. The four philosophical positions (Sera: lattice is natural/sacred, Torin: lattice is structure/tool, Kael: both sides are impositions, Veraine [absent]: lattice is disease) all have Codex-level support. The debate should feel genuinely unresolved.
